analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds a paragraph at head lines 1287-1300 describing the coordinator chunk send path. The documented path is ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler encrypting each SSE frame, then SendHandle.sendChunk, then the ChunkBatcher serial queue, then ChunkFrameWriter. SendHandle.send flushes queued frames before a terminal message. ChunkBatcher.enqueue drops a frame immediately when no session sink is bound. CoordinatorClient+Connection unbinds the old session on teardown, and ProviderLoop+Cancellation cancels in-flight requests separately.

No code, config, crypto or boundary behavior changes in the supplied evidence, so there is no direct security regression. The paragraph does record a security-relevant caveat: SendHandle and ChunkSender persist across reconnects, and the sink check runs when the enqueue closure executes. An old request's frame that is processed after a replacement sink binds therefore still passes the check, and nothing enforces request-to-session identity. The frames are already encrypted per request (T-008, TB-002), so this would not expose plaintext. A stale frame could still reach the coordinator on a new session, where the coordinator would need to reject it by request ID or session. That coordinator-side check is outside the supplied evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.

The next review pass should confirm in the actual Swift source (ChunkBatcher.swift, CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift, ProviderLoop+Cancellation.swift) that cancellation ordering prevents stale frames after reconnect, and that the coordinator ignores frames for unknown or cancelled request IDs. The rest of the document, unchanged GLM, calibration and deadline text, is not modified by this PR. The T-041 prefix-cache context is not affected.
